proof_boundary: The exact identities expose a finite natural-mollifier norm and a totally nonnegative max-kernel discrepancy energy. They do not prove the required uniform bound, RH, or Lambda<=0. Fixed-shift and cofinal equivalences are internally audited theorem candidates requiring independent review.

rows.proof_boundary: Absolute Dirichlet-series identity only.
rows.statement: For c_omega(n)=sum_(dm=n)mu(d)d^(-omega)m^omega, sum c_omega(n)n^(-s)=zeta(s-omega)/zeta(s+omega) when Re(s)>1+omega.

rows.proof_boundary: Definition and residue normalization only.
rows.statement: C_omega(x)=sum_(n<=x)c_omega(n), A_omega=1/((1+omega)zeta(1+2omega)), and E_omega(x)=C_omega(x)-A_omega*x^(1+omega).

rows.proof_boundary: Definition of the generalized fractional-part remainder.
rows.statement: R_omega(y)=sum_(m<=y)m^omega-y^(1+omega)/(1+omega), with R_omega(y)=-y^(1+omega)/(1+omega) for 0<y<1.

rows.proof_boundary: The d>x tail is part of the identity and must not be dropped.
rows.statement: E_omega(x)=sum_(d>=1)mu(d)d^(-omega)R_omega(x/d).

rows.proof_boundary: Pointwise absolute tail convergence is not Hilbert convergence.
rows.statement: For d>x the summand is -mu(d)x^(1+omega)/((1+omega)d^(1+2omega)); hence the tail is absolutely convergent for omega>0.

rows.proof_boundary: This concerns the base remainder, not the infinite Mobius sum.
rows.statement: R_omega(y)=O_omega(y^omega) at infinity and is -y^(1+omega)/(1+omega) below one, so R_omega belongs to H=L2((0,infinity),dx/x^2) exactly in the needed range 0<omega<1/2.

rows.proof_boundary: Generalized Muntz transform in its honest convergence strip.
rows.statement: Integral_0^infinity R_omega(x)x^(-s)dx/x =zeta(s-omega)/s for omega<Re(s)<1+omega.

rows.proof_boundary: Unitary orbit identity only.
rows.statement: U_d f(x)=sqrt(d)f(x/d) is unitary on H, and d^(-omega)R_omega(x/d)=d^(-omega-1/2)U_dR_omega(x).

rows.proof_boundary: Every E_(omega,N) is a finite H vector.
rows.statement: E_(omega,N)=sum_(d<=N)mu(d)d^(-omega)R_omega(x/d).

rows.proof_boundary: Finite Dirichlet polynomial; no limiting interchange is used.
rows.statement: On Re(s)=1/2, Mellin(E_(omega,N))(s)=zeta(s-omega)M_N(s+omega)/s, where M_N(u)=sum_(d<=N)mu(d)d^(-u).

rows.proof_boundary: Exact finite-N norm, not a bound uniform in N.
rows.statement: ||E_(omega,N)||_H^2=(1/(2pi))integral_R |zeta(1/2-omega+it)/(1/2+it)|^2|M_N(1/2+omega+it)|^2dt.

rows.proof_boundary: An exact weighted natural-mollifier norm on a line right of one half.
rows.statement: The functional equation rewrites the integrand as W_omega(t)|zeta(sigma+it)M_N(sigma+it)|^2, sigma=1/2+omega and W_omega(t)=|chi(1/2-omega+it)|^2/|1/2+it|^2.

rows.proof_boundary: Pointwise convergence does not imply H convergence.
rows.statement: E_(omega,N)(x) tends pointwise to E_omega(x) because the tail after d>x is absolutely convergent.

rows.proof_boundary: One-way handoff; no Bessel property is assumed.
rows.statement: sup_N ||E_(omega,N)||_H<infinity implies E_omega in H by Fatou and the pointwise limit.

rows.proof_boundary: Exact removal of the harmless negative-log-time tail.
rows.statement: E_omega in H iff J_omega=integral_1^infinity |E_omega(x)|^2dx/x^2<infinity, since the known x<1 contribution is A_omega^2/(1+2omega).

rows.proof_boundary: The second term removes the residue-main-term pole at s=1+omega.
rows.statement: For s=z+1/2, the positive-time transform is G_omega(s)=zeta(s-omega)/(s*zeta(s+omega))-A_omega/(s-1-omega), initially for Re(s)>1-omega.

rows.proof_boundary: Finite boundary energy does not prove positive-time Hardy support.
rows.statement: G_omega(1/2+it) is in L2(dt) after removable boundary zeros: the zeta-ratio term is O(|t|^(omega-1)) and omega<1/2.

rows.proof_boundary: Paley-Wiener implication; independent expert review required.
rows.statement: J_omega<infinity makes G_omega an H2 function in Re(s)>1/2; therefore every denominator zero in that half-plane is canceled and Suzuki's D(omega) holds.

rows.proof_boundary: Uses the audited fixed-shift innerness theorem and the standard gamma-quotient Hardy estimate.
rows.statement: If D(omega) holds, the completed quotient Q_omega is inner. The completed gamma quotient, its single removed pole, and the O(|t|^(omega-1)) boundary estimate put G_omega in H2, so transform uniqueness gives J_omega<infinity.

rows.proof_boundary: New corpus theorem candidate, not an unconditional J bound.
rows.statement: For every fixed 0<omega<1/2, J_omega<infinity iff D(omega).

rows.proof_boundary: Combines the fixed-shift candidate with the audited cofinal phase theorem.
rows.statement: RH iff there is a sequence omega_j->0 with integral_1^infinity |E_(omega_j)(x)|^2dx/x^2 finite for every j.

rows.proof_boundary: Conditional theorem technology; it cannot supply the missing unconditional bound.
rows.statement: Under RH, Balazard-Saias natural-Mobius approximation and Burnol's shifted-ratio estimate give E_(omega,N)->E_omega in H for every fixed 0<omega<1/2.

rows.proof_boundary: RH gives convergence; the reverse direction uses Fatou, the error-energy criterion, and cofinal accumulation.
rows.statement: RH iff there exist omega_j->0 such that sup_N ||E_(omega_j,N)||_H<infinity for every j.

rows.proof_boundary: All three terms must remain together.
rows.statement: For X>=1, J_omega(X)=integral_1^X E_omega(x)^2dx/x^2 equals sum_(n,m<=X)c_n*c_m*(1/max(n,m)-1/X)-(2A_omega/omega)sum_(n<=X)c_n*(X^omega-n^omega)+A_omega^2*(X^(1+2omega)-1)/(1+2omega).

rows.proof_boundary: Exact weighted H-minus-one discrepancy norm.
rows.statement: With eta_(omega,X)=sum_(n<=X)c_n delta_n-A_omega(1+omega)u^omega 1_(0,X](u)du, J_omega(X)=double_integral K_X(u,v)deta(u)deta(v), where K_X=1/max(1,u,v)-1/X on [0,X]^2.

rows.proof_boundary: Kernel total nonnegativity gives J>=0, not a uniform upper bound.
rows.statement: K_X(u,v)=integral_1^X 1_(u<=x)1_(v<=x)dx/x^2 is positive semidefinite; in reciprocal coordinates it is a Brownian min kernel and every ordered finite matrix is totally nonnegative by a cumulative-matrix factorization.

rows.proof_boundary: A proof using positivity of the max kernel alone cannot close the criterion.
rows.statement: The positive-positive, cross, and continuum-continuum pieces of the finite formula each have X^(1+2omega)-scale; only their signed combination can stay bounded.

rows.proof_boundary: Equal finite spectral energy does not distinguish the pole side; Hardy support does.
rows.statement: 1/(a+z) and 1/(a-z) have the same L2 boundary norm 1/(2a). The first is the transform of e^(-at)1_(t>0); the second has anti-causal boundary inverse e^(at)1_(t<0), while its actual positive-time Bromwich inverse is -e^(at).

rows.proof_boundary: Generic model v_d=v and coefficients 1/d is l2 while its vector partial sums diverge.
rows.statement: The coefficients d^(-omega-1/2) are square summable, but square-summable coefficients do not force convergence of a series of unit vectors without a Bessel bound.

rows.proof_boundary: Literature fit and proof template, not a transferred unconditional estimate.
rows.statement: Burnol's f_epsilon theorem has the same shifted-zeta-ratio, square-integrability, and causality architecture. The present R_omega identity is its fractional-power Jordan analogue.

rows.proof_boundary: The general closure theorem cannot be cited as the missing natural-mollifier bound.
rows.statement: Baez-Duarte's general strong Nyman-Beurling sufficiency requires compact support in the audited theorem, while R_omega is not compactly supported; arbitrary closure also does not prove convergence of this fixed natural Mobius series.

rows.proof_boundary: This all-height natural-mollifier estimate is not proved; finite t grids and finite X energies do not close it.
rows.statement: For one explicit omega_j->0, prove uniformly in N the exact finite inequality integral_R W_(omega_j)(t)|zeta(1/2+omega_j+it)M_N(1/2+omega_j+it)|^2dt<C_j.
